back2basics.text: Judicial review is the power of courts to examine the constitutionality and legality of executive and legislative actions. It ensures that government decisions comply with constitutional provisions and principles of fairness, transparency, and reasoned decision-making. This mechanism acts as a check on arbitrary or unlawful use of power by the state.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the Parandur airport project and the related PIL:

body.label: Project purpose
body.text: The ₹27,000 crore Parandur greenfield airport was planned to address a proven aviation capacity crunch at the existing Meenambakkam airport handling about 30 million passengers annually.

body.label: Land acquisition
body.text: The government had spent ₹680 crore to consolidate over 1,700 acres (48% of targeted land) in Kancheepuram district for the airport, with sanctioned acquisition of 1,527.32 hectares of private land and 798.12 hectares of government land.

body.label: Abandonment decision
body.text: In August 2026, the new Tamil Nadu government announced abandoning the project citing concerns over agricultural land acquisition and farmers' livelihoods, without presenting technical data or economic studies.

body.label: Constitutionality challenged
body.text: The PIL argues the abandonment decision is unconstitutional as it lacked any technical dataset, expert committee report, or comparative economic study.

body.label: Procedural irregularity
body.text: The Chief Minister made the announcement under Rule 110 of the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly Rules, which does not permit immediate debate, and the petitioner contends this use was illegal.

body.label: Interim reliefs sought
body.text: The petitioner seeks court directions to produce all internal files and reports related to the decision, an interim stay on the abandonment, and to restrain reclassification or transfer of acquired lands.

back2basics.concept: Electoral Roll Revision and Voter Inclusion
back2basics.text: Electoral rolls are periodically updated to include eligible voters and remove ineligible ones. The Election Commission of India conducts special enumeration phases to allow voters who were mistakenly deleted or newly eligible to apply for inclusion or correction. Forms such as Form 6 are for new voter registration, Form 8 for updating details, and enumeration forms for special cases. Judicial oversight ensures these processes are fair and accessible to all eligible voters.

2026-11-20-am-14e4204846.deck: The Supreme Court on November 19, 2026, urged voters deleted from electoral rolls to use all opportunities provided by the Election Commission of India (ECI) to get reincluded before the special enumeration phase ends on November 30. This is important for UPSC aspirants to understand ongoing electoral reforms, voter rights, and the judicial oversight of election processes.

back2basics.concept: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act, 1985
back2basics.text: The NDPS Act regulates the manufacture, possession, sale, transport, and consumption of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in India. It aims to prevent drug abuse and trafficking by imposing strict penalties for violations. Enforcement agencies like the DRI use this Act to seize illegal drugs and arrest offenders involved in illicit drug operations.

2026-11-20-am-29af08a172.deck: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI) recently seized large quantities of alprazolam intermediates and heroin in separate operations in Delhi and Chennai, arresting suspects involved in illicit drug manufacturing and trafficking. These actions highlight India's efforts to combat narcotics production and cross-border drug smuggling, relevant for internal security and law enforcement.

back2basics.text: A cyclone is a large-scale air mass that rotates around a strong center of low atmospheric pressure, often causing heavy rain and strong winds. Disaster management involves preparedness, response, and recovery measures to reduce the impact of such natural calamities. This includes early warning systems, evacuation plans, shelter arrangements, and coordination among various agencies to protect lives and property.

back2basics.text: Counter-terrorism involves coordinated actions by security agencies to prevent, detect, and respond to terrorist threats. It includes legal frameworks, intelligence sharing, operational capabilities, and addressing terror financing. A unified strategy ensures all agencies work together effectively, while proactive measures aim to dismantle terror networks before attacks occur.

back2basics.concept: Interim Bail and Legal Safeguards in Arrest
back2basics.text: Interim bail is a temporary relief granted by courts allowing an accused to be out of custody during trial or appeal. Legal safeguards such as those under Article 22(1) of the Constitution and Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act ensure proper procedure during arrest, including informing the arrested person of grounds and rights. back2basics.concept: Land Acquisition and Gram Sabha Consent
back2basics.text: The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 mandates that land acquisition in Scheduled Areas requires prior consent of the Gram Sabha, the village assembly of tribal communities. This protects tribal land rights by ensuring community approval before acquisition, especially for projects affecting their habitat and livelihood.

2026-11-20-am-d3d62d7983.deck: The Supreme Court ruled that prior consent of the Gram Sabha is mandatory for land acquisition in Scheduled Areas under the 2013 land acquisition law, setting aside Odisha's acquisition for a mining project. This judgment reinforces tribal land rights and impacts land acquisition and environmental governance policies.

back2basics.concept: Fiscal decentralisation and Panchayati Raj Institutions
back2basics.text: Fiscal decentralisation refers to the process of transferring financial powers and resources from the central or state governments to local bodies like Panchayats. Panchayati Raj Institutions are local self-government bodies in rural areas responsible for planning and implementing development programs. Their financial health depends on both intergovernmental transfers and own source revenues, which determine their capacity to deliver services.

2026-11-20-am-efc5ecdcc7.deck: The Reserve Bank of India released its second biennial report on the finances of Panchayati Raj Institutions, focusing on local finances and capacity building in rural India. This report is important for understanding fiscal decentralisation and rural governance finance in India.

body.label: Report scope
body.text: The report draws upon a balanced panel of 2.25 lakh Gram Panchayats covering 2022-23 to 2024-25 to assess their finances and role in rural socio-economic development.

body.label: Revenue sources
body.text: Gram Panchayats remain heavily dependent on intergovernmental transfers, which constitute about 90% of their total receipts, while own source revenues account for about 10%, mainly from non-tax sources like interest receipts, programme funds, and user charges.

body.label: Expenditure focus
body.text: Expenditure primarily reflects mandates of the Fifteenth Finance Commission and convergence with national schemes, with water supply and sanitation accounting for about 40% of total expenditure.

body.label: Progress and disparities
body.text: There has been notable progress in rural connectivity, electrification, water supply, sanitation, and community assets, but inter-State disparities persist in access, quality, and functionality.

body.label: Challenges in transition
body.text: As some large Gram Panchayats transition to small urban local bodies, their functional responsibilities may expand faster than their fiscal and administrative preparedness, requiring transitional fiscal support and capacity building.
